topicName: Fact Tables: Additive, Semi-Additive, and Non-Additive
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Fact Tables: Additive, Semi-Additive, and Non-Additive Measures"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In dimensional modeling and data warehousing, fact tables store quantitative metrics or measurements related to business events. Choosing the correct measure type is critical for ensuring accurate analytical reporting and preventing logical calculation errors."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Additive Measures"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Additive measures are metrics that can be aggregated across all dimensions in a data model. This means you can sum the values across time, location, product, and any other dimension without losing business context or mathematical accuracy."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examples: Sales Amount, Quantity Sold, Profit Margin, Shipping Cost."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"SELECT product_key, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales FROM fact_sales GROUP BY product_key;"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Semi-Additive Measures"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Semi-additive measures can be aggregated across some dimensions, but not all. Most commonly, they can be summed across dimensions like product or region, but cannot be meaningfully summed across the time dimension."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examples: Bank Account Balances, Inventory Levels, Headcount."},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you sum an account balance across 30 days of a month, you get a nonsensical figure. Instead, semi-additive measures over time require specific aggregation functions such as LAST, FIRST, or AVG."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT account_id, balance FROM fact_monthly_balance WHERE date_key = (SELECT MAX(date_key) FROM dim_date);"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Non-Additive Measures"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Non-additive measures cannot be aggregated using standard summation across any dimension. Summing these values yields mathematically invalid results. Instead, they require calculated averages, ratios, or distinct counts."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examples: Unit Prices, Ratios, Percentages, Temperature Readings."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you need to report on a non-additive measure like unit price across multiple products, you typically compute a weighted average rather than a direct sum."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SELECT SUM(sales_amount) / SUM(quantity_sold) AS weighted_average_price FROM fact_sales;"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary and Best Practices"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always identify the nature of your business metrics during the logical design phase."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Document aggregation rules in your BI semantic layer to prevent business users from running invalid SUM queries on semi-additive and non-additive data."}]
